subject: Privacy & Digital Rights
title: Police Use of Social Media
description: A tiny lesson with a big payoff: Police Use of Social Media.

hook.text: Police departments create fake social media profiles to monitor activists, protesters, and communities of color.

buildup.text: Law enforcement uses social media monitoring tools to track public posts, map networks, and predict behavior.

discovery.text: The NYPD monitored Black Lives Matter organizers on Facebook and Instagram, tracking their movements and plans.

twist.text: Social media companies' terms of service prohibit fake accounts. But they rarely enforce this against police.

climax.text: Your public posts become police intelligence. Free speech becomes evidence. Protest becomes probable cause.

punchline.text: Your posts. Their evidence. No warrant needed.

quiz.question: How have police used social media to surveil communities?
options: By creating fake profiles and using monitoring tools to track activists
By legally requesting all private messages from platforms
By sending friend requests from official department accounts
